folders.title: DP 1
folders.description:
1. Answer the set of questions about the following article:
Document 1 - “Proton Pump Inhibitor use increases mortality and hepatic decompensation in liver cirrhosis" tablet device – suggested time: 40mn
Of note: Proton Pump Inhibitor will be referred to as PPI

questions.question: Possible reason(s) to explain the higher mortality & increased occurrence of hepatic events with PPI could include
choix: A) Modification of gut PH, causing gut dysbiosis
B) Reduced hepatic clearance of PPI in the liver by cytochrome CYP450
C) PPIs limit the defense mechanism of hydrochloric acid
D) Increased risk of pathological bacterial translocation
E) PPIs break down all the ingested food, stopping the production of all stomach acid

questions.question: Limitation(s) identified in the text include(s):
choix: A) Selection bias where this is a single-center study, with unclear user definition
C) Overgeneralisation as the study ignores the potential benefits of PPIs
D) Transparency Concerns include no funding disclosure

questions.question: What was/ were the criterion/- ia used to define PPI users in the study of hospitalised cirrhotic patients?
choix: A) PPI use for at least 3 months prior to index admission
B) Cumulative Defined Daily Dose (cDDD) ≥ 28 within the landmark period
C) Patients with a PPI prescribed only after the landmark period
D) No PPI prescribed during the landmark period
E) PPI-prescribed patients with unclear indications

questions.question: Table 2 - In the 6-month landmark cohort, what was NOT/ were NOT the adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs) for overall mortality in PPI users compared to non-users?
In the study of patients with decompensated liver cirrhosis, what was/ were the Relative Risks (aRRs) of hospitalisation for hepatic decompensation in PPI users compared to non-users?
What type of study is this?
What is/ are the main measure (s) of association for the primary outcome?
What is a/ are key potential residual confounder(s) not fully addressed?
What is/ are the main take-home message(s) for clinical practice?
choix: A) PPIs are protective in cirrhosis
B) PPIs should not be used long-term in cirrhosis
C) PPI use should be regularly reviewed and minimised when not indicated
D) PPI use is not associated with any risks
E) PPI can be considered an option for patients waiting for orthotopic liver transplantation.
